resource.name: Invisible Illness — TOPx HHS 2026 Focus Area
resource.description: The Invisible Illness focus area is intentionally broad and inclusive. Invisible illness may include, but is not limited to, autoimmune conditions, mental health and behavioral health conditions, suicide prevention, Long COVID, myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS), infection-associated chronic conditions (IACCs), Lyme disease and other tickborne diseases, and other conditions that may not be immediately visible or outwardly apparent.

resource.name: Lyme Innovation — TOPx HHS 2026 Focus Area
resource.description: The TOPx HHS Tech Sprint for AI and Invisible Illness in 2026 is a four-month national competition with a $2,000,000 prize pool that puts U.S. open data in the hands of the public—mobilizing data enthusiasts, AI experts, technologists, entrepreneurs, and communities to build real-world tools using government data, American innovation, and AI to address the urgent health challenge with Lyme disease, alpha gal syndrome (AGS, the “meat allergy”), and other tickborne conditions.

resource.name: Cost of Illness — TOPx HHS 2026 Focus Area
resource.description: The Cost of Illness focus area explores both the economic and human burden of chronic disease and invisible illness. Participants may examine direct and indirect costs associated with delayed diagnosis, reduced workforce participation, care fragmentation, disability, caregiving, mental health burden, and barriers to accessing care and support services.
